content:
Water intelligence company WaterSense has
secured €5.75 million in funding through a combination of grants and a pre-seed
round co-led by b2venture and Movens Capital, with participation from
vastpoint. The new capital will support the expansion of its water monitoring
infrastructure across Europe.

Founded by Filip Budny, WaterSense develops
autonomous water quality monitoring technology that combines proprietary sensor
hardware with an AI-powered platform to help industrial operators, utilities
and public authorities monitor and manage water resources.

Water plays a critical role in industrial
production, cooling systems, wastewater management and public infrastructure.
As water supplies become increasingly constrained, water security is also
becoming a strategic priority for the European Union.

Despite its importance, water quality
monitoring still relies largely on manual sampling and laboratory analysis.
This process can take several days, providing only a snapshot of conditions at
a particular location and making it difficult to detect contamination and
respond in real time. Recent pollution incidents across European rivers,
including the Po, Vistula and Oder, have highlighted the limitations of
existing monitoring methods.

WaterSense aims to address these challenges
through an autonomous monitoring system based on technology developed by Budny
during his PhD research at Warsaw University of Technology. Conventional
sensor-based monitoring systems often face challenges related to biofouling,
high maintenance costs and complex servicing requirements, limiting their
widespread adoption.

WaterSense's technology uses hundreds of
low-cost miniature printed sensors that are automatically replaced daily. This
reduces maintenance requirements, prevents biofouling from limiting sensor
performance and enables continuous monitoring across a broader range of water
quality parameters.

The hardware is complemented by an AI-native
platform that integrates real-time measurements into customers' existing
systems and operational workflows. Deep-learning models predict changes in
water quality up to 72 hours in advance, while satellite data extends
monitoring coverage beyond individual measurement locations. AI agents analyse
the collected data to provide alerts, insights and operational decision
support.

WaterSense currently monitors more than 80
locations for over 30 customers across four countries, covering environments
ranging from alpine lakes in Austria to urban water systems in major European
cities. Through its Data-as-a-Service model, the company provides customers
with continuous access to water quality data without requiring them to develop
their own monitoring infrastructure.

As adoption grows, each deployment
contributes to a broader dataset covering different water bodies, geographical
regions and operating conditions, supporting the development of the platform's
predictive capabilities.

The new funding will be used to expand
WaterSense's monitoring network across European rivers, lakes and water
systems, moving beyond individual monitoring locations towards system-wide
water intelligence. A planned full rollout along the Oder River will be one of
the company's next major steps.

WaterSense will also continue expanding its
European deployments and developing its data infrastructure, predictive models
and operational decision-support capabilities.
